title: Sales Associate (Part-Time), Los Angeles
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.




ALSO is looking for a Part-Time Sales Associate to support the launch and growth of our brand in/around Los Angeles. This is a field-based, customer-facing role that works closely with and reports to the Market Manager to bring ALSO to life through mobile demos, retail experiences, and community activations. You’ll be on the front lines—introducing customers to our vehicles, delivering exceptional experiences, and helping build the foundation of ALSO’s presence in Los Angeles.

This role is ideal for someone who is energetic, people-oriented, and excited to be part of an early-stage brand with room to grow.

 

What You Will Do

Customer Experience & Sales Support

 - Deliver engaging, high-quality customer experiences in both mobile and fixed retail environments.

 - Educate customers on ALSO vehicles, features, and benefits, guiding them through demo rides and early purchase consideration.

 - Support local sales goals by converting interest into qualified leads and sales.

 - Share customer feedback and insights with the Market Manager to improve execution and experiences.

Mobile Demo & Event Support

 - Assist with the setup, execution, and breakdown of mobile demo experiences and local activation events, including driving the custom Rivian EV van to/from events.

 - Safely operate and maintain the local demo fleet, ensuring vehicles are clean, charged, and customer-ready.

 - Represent ALSO at community events, pop-ups, and partner activations.

Retail Store Operations (in applicable markets, over time)

 - Support daily retail hub operations, including opening and closing procedures, merchandising, and general upkeep.

 - Deliver best-in-class customer service and demonstrate active selling skills.

 - Help create a welcoming, on-brand environment that reflects ALSO’s premium and playful ethos.

Operational Support

 - Follow operational, safety, and compliance processes as directed by the Market Manager and/or Market Coordinator.
   
   
   

What You Will Bring

 - 1+ years of experience in retail, events, sales, hospitality, brand ambassador, or customer-facing roles.

 - A positive, proactive attitude and willingness to jump in wherever needed - you actively engage in your professional development.

 - Strong interpersonal and communication skills—you enjoy talking to people, telling a compelling story, and actively selling products and services.

 - Ability to work in a dynamic, field-based environment, including weekends and events - you have a flexible work style and enjoy variety in your work schedule.

 - Interest in cycling, electric vehicles and/or innovative consumer brands - your enthusiasm for our brand is infectious!

 - Ability to work collaboratively while also taking direction and feedback well - you are a charismatic and fun team player!

 - A strong connection to, knowledge of and comfort riding a bike in Los Angeles is a plus!

 - Qualify as an authorized driver, meaning you are at least 21 years of age, have a valid U.S. driver’s license with a minimum of three (3) years of licensed driving experience, and can successfully complete a background screening and motor vehicle review - because you’ll be driving our demo van and fleet of bikes to meet customers where they like to ride!
   
   
   

This position offers an hourly pay rate of $21.00 per hour and is eligible to participate in the sales incentive program in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan. This role is expected to work approximately 20–24 hours per week. As a part-time position working fewer than 30 hours per week, this role is not eligible for company-sponsored benefits.

Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

The Director, Search & Evaluation and Strategy of Neuroscience will identify, evaluate, and advance external innovation opportunities while contributing to the development and execution of therapeutic-area Business Development strategy. This role will connect portfolio and pipeline priorities with actionable external search plans, rigorous opportunity assessments, and transaction support. description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules to Late Stage Clinical.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
This Senior Scientist – Solid State Characterization position will be in a technical specialty group - Physical Analytical Chemistry (PAC) withing Analytical R&D.  The PAC group is a global team of experienced and innovative scientists which utilize a diverse set of physical analytical tools to advance CMC development programs by providing insights and driving the understanding of materials, processes, and products.  Additionally, the group contributes to development and justification of control strategies and authors relevant sections of regulatory submissions across all development phases.
We are looking for a subject matter expert in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of drug substances (DS) and drug products (DP), from early form discovery through regulatory filing. The role focuses on single crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), electron diffraction (3D ED/MicroED), Rietveld refinement, quantitative phase analysis (QPA), and phase-appropriate polymorph quantitation methods both in drug substance and drug products. The scientist will work closely with Molecular Profiling Drug Development, Process Chemistry, Formulation, Process Engineering, Analytical, Operations, Quality Assurance and CMC-Regulatory.
Key Responsibilities:
Support new product development with advanced methods development and validations, technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements.
Serve as technical SME in X-ray and electron diffraction for crystallographic and solid-form characterization of DS and DP; Responsible for PXRD method development for DS and DP, validation/technical transfer packages, and generation of technical data in support regulatory requirements
Serve as the PXRD expert for supporting solid form screening, identification, crystallinity, and stability studies; perform indexing, Pawley/Le Bail fitting, Rietveld refinement, and structure determination from powder data.
Perform quantitative phase analysis: Quantify polymorphic and amorphous content in DS and DP using Rietveld, whole-pattern, and multivariate approaches, addressing low drug load, excipient interference, preferred orientation, and micro absorption.
Apply advanced diffraction such as VT/VH-XRPD, in situ, synchrotron, and PDF analysis to study phase transformations and poorly crystalline/amorphous materials.
Apply SCXRD and 3D ED/MicroED structure determination, including absolute configuration and crystal packing of APIs, salts, cocrystals, hydrates, and solvates; generate calculated powder patterns and CIF reports.
Conduct orthogonal solid-state characterization including X-ray diffraction, thermal analysis, moisture sorption, microscopy, spectroscopy as applicable for solid form, impurity and stability studies
Support solid form control strategies per ICH Q6A, author Module 3 sections and health authority responses, and ensure GMP and data integrity compliance.
Highly autonomous and productive in performing laboratory work, method development and troubleshoot; processing, interpreting, and visualizing data to facilitate project team decisions
Represent PAC on CMC teams, lead form-change investigations, mentor scientists, and implement new diffraction technologies.
Build strong relationships with peers and cross functionally with partners outside of team to enable higher performance.
Routinely demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in research or development activities and maintain a high level of productivity in the lab.
Understand and adhere to corporate standards regarding code of conduct, safety, appropriate handling of materials, controlled drug and radioactive compounds, and GxP compliance, where applicable.
Qualifications:
Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in Chemistry, Material Science, Physics, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field typically with minimum 10 (BS), 8 (MS), or 0 – 2 (Ph.D.) years related industry experience.
Strong technical background in solid state characterization, excellent analytical problem-solving, communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills. Capable of independently developing and troubleshoot analytical methods.
Extensive hands-on PXRD experience, including indexing, Rietveld refinement, QPA, and polymorph and amorphous quantitation.
Track record of developing and validating PXRD methods for DS and DP in a GMP environment, with knowledge of ICH Q2(R2), Q6A, Q14, and USP .
Expertise in small molecule SCXRD structure solution and refinement, including disorder modeling and absolute structure; and knowledge of 3D ED/MicroED approaches.
Proficiency with tools such as Olex2, SHELX, CrysAlisPro, TOPAS, Diffrac Eva and DQuant, GSAS-II, HighScore, Mercury, and the CSD.
Hands-on experience with DSC, TGA, hot-stage and polarized light microscopy, DVS, and strong data analysis and interpretation skills.
Experience with Raman/FTIR/NIR, solid-state NMR, SEM, SAXS, micro-CT, and crystal structure prediction, and particle characterization is preferred.
Experience with AI/ML and data science for automation of phase identification and Rietveld/QPA workflows, chemometrics, and Python or R scripting is preferred.
Experience with biophysical characterization tools of nanoDSC, DLS, SEC-MALS, CD, AUC, nanoDSF in peptide, LNP and biologic materials, formulations and process characterization is preferred.
Strong pharmaceutical industry experience in solid state characterization is preferred
Ability to coordinate activities and work simultaneously on multiple projects, in a global, fast-paced setting where priorities may change quickly.
High attention to detail and creative problem solving while exhibiting strong interpersonal skills and proven ability to work independently as well as part of cross functional teams
Knowledge of instrument set-up, troubleshooting, management and maintenance.
Experience extracting insights from multidimensional data sets, along with other physical analytical characterizations, and connecting to pharmaceutical materials, processes, and products
Practical knowledge of organic structure, functional groups, chemistry, and modern spectroscopic techniques as applied to small-molecule analytical analysis.
Create a learning environment, open to suggestions and experimentation for improvement.
Embrace the ideas of others, nurture innovation and manage innovation to reality.

description:

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Power & Hydrogen Program Manager, Power & Hydrogen Solutions, GESA
description:
An execution-focused project/program manager responsible for the hands-on coordination and completion of power capacity and hydrogen fuel cell projects across the Amazon fulfillment network. This is a delivery role with a strong bias for action: the PM owns the details, gets into the field, and drives projects from feasibility through commissioning and handover. Oversees multiple concurrent projects spanning temporary and permanent power deployment (utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and air permitting) as well as hydrogen fuel cell execution — including decommissioning of existing assets, launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes, and conversions of existing sites. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, and personally tracks and unblocks progress. Prepares reports for upper management regarding the status of all projects.
Requires a bachelor's degree and at least 4 years of project management experience in power infrastructure, electrical systems, hydrogen/fuel cell systems, or a related area. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, detail-oriented operator who thrives in ambiguity, dives deep into technical and schedule details, and acts with urgency rather than waiting for direction. Must be familiar with a variety of the field's concepts, practices, and procedures across both power and hydrogen domains. Relies on sound judgment to plan and accomplish goals, and is comfortable rolling up sleeves — walking the site, reading the drawings, chasing the long-lead order, and closing out the punch list. Leads and directs the work of contractors, vendors, and cross-functional teams. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected to solve complex energy infrastructure challenges across diverse site conditions and regulatory environments. Typically reports to a manager or head of a unit/department.
Key job responsibilities
Project Management & Bias for Action
• Own delivery end to end and act with urgency — move projects forward every day rather than waiting for direction or escalation
• Get into the details: read the drawings, interrogate the schedule, understand the single-line and the hydrogen P&ID, and verify the numbers personally
• Be hands-on and in the field — walk the site, attend installation and commissioning activities, and verify work directly rather than relying solely on status reports
• Build and maintain the plan of record: detailed schedules, critical-path analysis, dependencies, risks, and clear owners and dates
• Proactively identify blockers and drive them to closure; dive deep on root cause and remove obstacles for contractors and cross-functional teams
• Run a tight operating rhythm — stand-ups, weekly reviews, and crisp written updates that make status and risks unambiguous
• Make decisions with incomplete information, bias toward action, and course-correct quickly as new data emerges
Program Coordination & Oversight
• Responsible for the coordination and completion of multiple simultaneous power and hydrogen execution projects across U.S. sites
• Oversee all aspects of the execution program from feasibility through commissioning and handover
• Set deadlines, assign responsibilities, and monitor and summarize the progress of all projects
• Prepare reports for upper management regarding program status, including monthly flash updates and executive summaries
• Lead and direct the work of contractors, vendors, consultants, and cross-functional teams
• Perform a variety of tasks ranging from technical design review to stakeholder management to regulatory coordination
Amazon Standards, Specifications & Quality Assurance
• Follow and verify that Amazon standards, specifications, and processes are met across all power and hydrogen infrastructure installations
• Ensure electrical equipment, switchgear, generators, fuel cells, hydrogen storage/dispensing systems, and associated systems comply with Amazon technical standards and design requirements
• Conduct quality reviews at each project phase to validate adherence to Amazon specifications before progressing to the next milestone
• Verify vendor deliverables, shop drawings, and equipment submittals meet Amazon engineering standards
• Coordinate with Amazon internal engineering teams to resolve specification questions and obtain approvals
• Document and track any deviations from Amazon specifications, securing proper waivers or corrective actions (e.g., Supplier Corrective Action Reports / SCARs)
Power Capacity Execution
• Drive execution of temporary and permanent power deployment projects — utility upgrades, generator installations, switchgear deployments, and service upgrades
• Oversee deployment of temporary and permanent natural gas and diesel generator systems (1–5MW scale), including rental genset mobilization and conversion to permanent power
• Manage utility coordination including transformer upgrades, switchgear installations, and service upgrades with utility companies
• Own the end-to-end switchgear (SWGR) procurement process: specification development, vendor selection, purchase order issuance, and delivery tracking
• Track SWGR lead times (typically 10–26 weeks) across all sites and ensure orders are placed to meet project timelines; monitor factory acceptance testing (FAT) and coordinate site delivery logistics
• Review and validate electrical designs, single-line diagrams, load calculations, and power distribution configurations
• Ensure compliance with NEC, NFPA, and local electrical codes
Hydrogen Fuel Cell Execution
• Decommissioning: Plan and execute safe decommissioning of existing hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cell assets — isolation, purging/inerting, asset removal, site restoration, and disposition in accordance with Amazon standards and applicable safety codes
• Infrastructure & fuel cell launch: Lead the launch of new hydrogen infrastructure and fuel cells per Amazon standards and processes — hydrogen storage and dispensing systems, hydrogen pads, piping, fueling infrastructure, and fuel cell power modules, from design review through installation, commissioning, and startup
• Conversions: Manage conversions of existing sites to hydrogen fuel cell operation (or between configurations), coordinating the transition sequencing, infrastructure modifications, and cutover to minimize operational disruption
• Coordinate with hydrogen fuel cell vendors and OEMs (e.g., Plug Power and equivalents) on equipment specifications, delivery schedules, and field support
• Verify hydrogen systems meet Amazon specifications and applicable hydrogen safety and fire codes (e.g., NFPA 2, NFPA 55) throughout design, installation, and commissioning
• Oversee fuel cell capacity planning, dispenser configuration, and integration with site power and operations
Procurement & Long-Lead Equipment Management
• Own procurement for long-lead equipment across both domains — switchgear, generators, fuel cells, and hydrogen infrastructure components
• Specify, order, track lead times, verify specifications, and coordinate delivery for critical-path equipment
• Coordinate with manufacturers and vendors on custom configurations and delivery schedules
• Escalate equipment delivery risks immediately when lead times threaten project schedules
Permitting & Regulatory
• Own the permitting process for all sites — air permit applications for stationary generator installations and hydrogen-related permits and approvals
• Prepare and submit permit applications across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments; track application status, agency review timelines, and approval milestones for each site
• Navigate complex permitting scenarios including CEQA approvals, non-attainment areas, emission offset requirements, and hydrogen/fire code approvals
• Coordinate with environmental and fire/life-safety consultants to develop applications, emission calculations, and hazard analyses
• Maintain a permit tracking log with submission dates, agency contacts, expected approval dates, and required follow-ups
• Proactively identify permitting risks and develop contingency plans to avoid schedule impacts; ensure all required emission and safety data is obtained from generator and fuel cell vendors
Project Execution & Delivery
• Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle: feasibility, design, procurement, permitting, installation, commissioning, and handover
• Develop and maintain detailed project schedules, budgets, risk registers, and status reports
• Coordinate contractor mobilization, equipment procurement, and installation activities
• Identify and resolve critical-path blockers with urgency; escalate issues proactively
• Rely on extensive experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals under compressed timelines
Stakeholder Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact and single-threaded owner across all project stakeholders, aligning internal and external parties and holding each accountable to deliverables and timelines
• Customer — Amazon Operations: partner with Amazon Operations (the internal customer) to understand site requirements, manage expectations, minimize operational disruption, and secure buy-in through launch and handover
• General Contractor (GC): direct and hold the GC accountable for construction scope, schedule, RFIs, submittals, and field execution
• Engineer of Record (EOR) & Architect of Record (AOR): coordinate design intent, drawing reviews, RFIs, and design changes; ensure the installed work conforms to the stamped design
• Electrical Contractor (EC): coordinate electrical installation, terminations, testing, and energization activities and sequencing
• Air permitting agencies & consultants: engage regulatory agencies and environmental consultants (e.g., Trinity) to secure and maintain air permits and keep applications on the critical path
• Utility engagement — gas pipeline: drive utility coordination for natural gas pipeline connections, metering, pressure requirements, service applications, and interconnection timelines
• Equipment vendors & OEMs: manage generator, switchgear, fuel cell, and hydrogen infrastructure vendors on specifications, lead times, and field support
• Coordinate with Property/Construction Managers (PCMs) and Construction Managers at each site
• Provide weekly status updates and monthly program reports to leadership
Site Launches, Commissioning & Energization
• Travel to project sites during critical installation, commissioning, and decommissioning phases
• Oversee equipment startup, testing, and acceptance procedures for both power and hydrogen systems
• Ensure safe energization, hydrogen system startup, and transition to operations

- 4+ years of defining and executing against program timeline & requirements experience

- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

title: AI Applied Scientist, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function, it is a foundational science. Our team, part of Apple Services Engineering, is building that scientific foundation: rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology for LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will work alongside measurement scientists (psychometrics, validity theory), ML researchers, and platform engineers, bringing together ML research, statistical rigor, and production engineering.
We are looking for an Applied Scientist who works across the full arc of evaluation science: turning research into tools engineers can use on their own, and turning what those engineers run into new research. You care whether a method holds up on real data, at real scale, for a real decision, and you are curious enough to go after the open question underneath when it doesn't.
Our team is building self-service evaluation: tools, SDKs, and AI-powered capabilities that let engineers across Apple evaluate their AI features on their own, quickly and correctly, so they can build and ship those features faster. You will develop the methods that make this possible: raising the quality of the evaluations engineers run, and helping them understand what their results mean and what to do next. Often the method a problem needs doesn't exist yet. When that happens, you will figure it out, whether that means extending a recent paper or developing something new, and share what you learn through publications and internal research reports. We are looking for individuals across a range of experience levels.
With research and measurement scientists, you will co-develop new methods, make sure the tools give engineers valid, trustworthy signals, and bring back the hard problems that should shape the team's research agenda. With platform and research engineers, you will define what each method needs to work reliably without an expert in the loop, including its assumptions, failure modes, and validation tests, so it can ship in the evaluation SDKs and APIs used across Apple.
The successful candidate combines scientific depth with practical judgment: you know which methods fit a problem and why, can design experiments that show whether they actually work, can diagnose why they break down on messy real-world data, and can explain clearly what an evaluation result does and does not support.
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field, or a Master's degree in one of these fields with 3+ years of applied research experience.
Deep expertise in evaluating AI systems, gained through research on evaluation methods, substantial hands-on experience evaluating LLMs or agentic systems in real products, or both.
Strong proficiency in Python and the modern ML ecosystem, with demonstrated ability to implement complex methods from recent papers and run large-scale experiments.
Hands-on experience with large language models, whether fine-tuning, inference, prompting pipelines, or building LLM-powered applications.
Demonstrated research ability through publications at peer-reviewed venues, preprints, or equivalent research output.
Track record of applying research to practical problems: methods, prototypes, or tools adopted by other teams or used to inform real product decisions.
Solid software engineering fundamentals for research code: version control, testing, reproducibility, and code others can build on.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex results, and their limitations, to diverse audiences.
Comfort with ambiguity and new problem spaces; you thrive when building something that doesn't yet have a playbook.
Preferred qualifications: First-author publications at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP), especially on evaluation methodology: papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation to demonstrate model improvements.
Specific experience in one or more of: LLM-as-judge approaches (calibration, rubric design, bias mitigation); benchmark design and validation (IRT, contamination detection); human evaluation methodology (protocol design, quality control); experimentation and comparisons between system versions (A/B testing, uncertainty quantification); or agentic and multi-agent system evaluation, including failure diagnosis and automated red-teaming.
Familiarity with theoretical foundations of evaluation: measurement theory and validity frameworks, statistical learning theory (calibration, reliability, decision theory), causal inference, or preference aggregation.
Experience with the practical challenges of evaluating generative AI and agentic systems: non-deterministic outputs, token economics, multi-turn agent trajectories, and tool use.
Experience building methods or tools used directly by non-experts, such as developer-facing ML tooling or self-service analytics.
Familiarity with modern evaluation tools and frameworks (e.g., DeepEval, Ragas, TruLens, LangSmith, or agent tracing and observability tools).
Experience working with distributed computing or cloud-native tooling (e.g., Ray, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes) to run evaluations at scale.
Experience with cross-disciplinary work, such as collaboration with social scientists, psychometricians, or domain experts.
Experience in fast-moving, early-stage teams where you helped define technical direction from the ground up.

title: Senior Research Manager, AI Evaluation Science
description:
AI systems are only as trustworthy as the methods used to evaluate them. At Apple, where AI powers experiences for billions of people, getting evaluation right is not a support function. It is a foundational science. As these systems grow in complexity, the quality of our products is increasingly constrained by the quality of our evaluation methods. Our team is building the scientific foundation and self-service tools for how AI evaluation is done at scale, spanning LLMs, agentic systems, and human-AI interaction. Our goal is evidence that teams can act on: what to measure, whether a change helped, why a system failed, and whether it is ready to ship. We don’t just publish methods; we productionize them. We are looking for a Sr. Research Manager to lead an interdisciplinary research team that advances the state-of-the-art in evaluation methods that can be shipped as production tools for Apple developers and published in top venues.
We are looking for a Sr. Research Manager to lead an interdisciplinary research team advancing the frontier of evaluation methods. The team works in close collaboration with applied scientists and measurement scientists to build evaluation methodology and systems that are human-centered, psychometrically rigorous, and technically frontier. You will set the research agenda, direct the team's portfolio across near-term and long-term bets, and ensure that novel methods are designed from the outset for productionization into evaluation SDKs and APIs. You will have a strong background in ML or a closely related quantitative field and a track record of leading research teams that publish at top venues while simultaneously shipping methods into production tools.
What makes this team unusual is its interdisciplinary core. You will lead ML researchers, measurement scientists, and applied scientists, bringing together frontier ML research, psychometric and statistical rigor, and production engineering. What unites the strongest candidates is depth of thinking about evaluation as a research problem and the conviction that how we measure AI systems is as important as how we build them.
Minimum qualifications: Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a closely related field
5+ years of experience managing or leading research teams in an industry setting, with demonstrated ability to attract and retain strong research talent
Experience publishing research at top-tier AI/ML venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP) or comparable venues in statistics or measurement
Experience partnering with applied science and engineering teams to translate research into production systems, tools, or capabilities adopted by others
Technical depth in AI evaluation, with the ability to critically assess and advance methods for measuring AI system behavior, whether through automated judgment, benchmark design, synthetic data, human evaluation, experimentation, failure analysis, or other approaches
Demonstrated ability to set research strategy, manage a research portfolio with competing priorities, and make disciplined investment decisions across near-term and long-term work
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to represent research to executive leadership, partner teams, and the external research community
Preferred qualifications: Ability to bridge ML research and measurement science. This could mean a machine learning background with genuine familiarity with validity and evaluation design, or a measurement science background with strong technical depth in ML methods
Publications or demonstrated expertise specifically in evaluation methodology (papers about how to evaluate, not just papers that use evaluation)

title: Senior Software Engineer — Streaming Speech Translation Data
description:
We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to architect, build, and scale our end-to-end streaming speech translation data pipelines. In this role, you will own the infrastructure and data workflows that transform raw multilingual data into high-quality training and evaluation datasets for real-time speech-to-speech and speech-to-text foundation models.
You will work at the intersection of distributed systems, large-scale data engineering, and generative AI—integrating LLM APIs, forced alignment, text normalization, and GPU-accelerated Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesis into resilient, high-throughput pipelines.
You will be part of a team that's responsible for a wide variety of language technologies related development activities. Your focus will be on developing the model automation pipelines which are highly scalable, robust and efficient. The role will be part of the model automation team to deal with large quantities of data, apply the state-of-the-art methods in deep learning to tackle real world problems, create the production quality models at scale and set up ML CI/CD pipelines.
Minimum qualifications: Experience:5+ years of industry experience building large-scale distributed data pipelines, backend systems, or ML infrastructure.
Distributed Computing:Strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience with distributed processing frameworks and modern data lakehouse formats.
GPU & Model Serving Integration: Experience orchestrating GPU-accelerated workloads and managing high-concurrency API calls with robust rate-limiting, retry, and batching strategies.
Speech/NLP Fundamentals:Practical understanding of audio data processing, forced alignment, and multilingual text processing pipelines.
Engineering Rigor:Proven track record of owning production systems end-to-end, including monitoring, automated testing, CI/CD, and debugging complex distributed bottlenecks.
Preferred qualifications: Direct experience with speech-to-speech translation, streaming ASR/TTS, or forced alignment.
Familiarity with text normalization and inverse text normalization across diverse languages and scripts.
Experience optimizing GPU utilization for batch audio synthesis and inference.
Background in building automated data quality scoring and filtering pipelines for speech or text corpora.

title: Senior Software Engineer, System Performance
description:
The cloudOS Engineering team is looking for an exceptional system software engineer with a focus on performance to develop and optimize software and services that power the next generation of server platforms powering Apple Services.
In this highly collaborative role, you will be at the center of multiple efforts that utilize hardware acceleration for machine learning and high-performance computing workloads hosted on Apple’s Private Cloud Compute Infrastructure and powering pivotal end-user experiences such as Apple Intelligence. You will be part of a team whose work spans across the stack, from firmware to the full stack of software and application services. You will partner with teams across Apple to adapt, tailor, and scale software and influence hardware platforms for novel compute platforms and will help to build the foundation of our future cloud architecture.
We are looking for someone with proven mastery at understanding performance-critical interactions and building scalable, highly performant, energy-efficient systems.
The cloudOS System Performance team is responsible for developing software, services and tools that enable our clients to build and run highly available, performant and scalable software for all our supported OSes.
We do this by building observability to identify aspects that are critical to performance and then driving efforts to optimize for performance. We work across the software and services stack, collaborating with teams who develop and run services for Apple as well as core platform teams responsible for providing the OS. We leverage the experience gained from this collaborative process of continuous improvement to influence our partner teams in hardware, architecture, software and services areas to share future platforms to meet our customer needs.
This is a unique opportunity to work across the firmware, software and services areas in Apple’s data-center platform stack. This role will entail identifying, isolating and resolving aspects of systems performance across all layers of the stack from microcontroller firmware level all the way up to the services application layer. You will work in a collaborative, fast-paced team, delving into areas across the software and services stack, with the goal of maximizing the operational capacity and efficiency for the platform.
We're looking for someone with a strong foundation in systems programming, a genuine interest and curiousity in the area of system performance paired with the drive to learn quickly and join a high-paced and experienced team.
You should have a strong mix of education and practical experience with a real passion for diving head first into challenging problems.
You are skilled at the art of communicating and enjoy it.

Bachelors or Masters in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience.
Experience in developing System Software.
Strong knowledge of Operating Systems and Computer Architecture.
Passion for Building and Optimizing High Performance, Energy Efficient Services (at Data-Center Scale).
Excellent communication skills.
Creative, collaborative, and product-focused.

Familiarity with performance aspects of virtualization and containerization technologies.
Experience with building performance-oriented observability services.
Experience with building software to optimize for perf/watt and perf/capacity.
Experience with Linux-based AI accelerator (GPUs, TPUs, ASICs) platforms.

title: Senior Software Engineer: CloudOS Build Quality and Release
description:
Apple Service Engineering is seeking an exceptional Senior Software Release Engineer for a high-visibility, high-impact role at the center of our next-generation datacenter and cloudOS initiatives.
This role is for a senior engineer who wants to define how world-class distributed systems are built, tested, validated, and released at scale. You will be a technical leader and key contributor to the foundation of Apple's future cloud architecture, working directly with the systems that power Apple Intelligence and Private Cloud Compute.
You will drive critical testing, validation, and release initiatives across highly performant, energy-efficient platforms built on Apple Silicon. You will play a central role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and scalability of datacenter technology that reaches hundreds of millions of people.
As a Senior Software Release Engineer on the cloudOS release team, you will drive the test strategy, automation infrastructure, and validation frameworks behind some of Apple's most critical and technically complex distributed systems.
You will work at the intersection of hardware and software, across the full stack, to ensure that next-generation datacenter technology is performant, reliable, and ready to scale. You will bring senior-level technical leadership to every initiative you own, from defining test architecture to resolving the most complex system-level issues. You will partner with hardware, platform, architecture, and SOC architecture teams, as well as software teams across Apple, to adapt, validate, and scale software on novel compute platforms before they reach production. You will also build the tooling and automation frameworks that lets the broader engineering organization move with speed and confidence.

8+ years of experience in software quality engineering, release engineering, or build and release management.

title: Software Engineering Manager, AIML — LLM Inference Quality
description:
Apple is building the next generation of AI data center infrastructure to power large language model (LLM) services at scale. We are looking for a hands-on engineering manager to lead the team that owns the Quality, correctness, consistency, and stability of LLM inference in production.
Your team builds the automation frameworks, evaluation methodology, and qualification strategy that give Apple confidence in every model, prompt, serving stack, and infrastructure change before it reaches users. This is the safety net that lets Apple ship frontier AI quickly — without sacrificing quality, safety, or trust. We are seeking a deeply experienced manager who stays close to the technology to drive both the technical roadmap and the delivery of a high-performing team.
As a technical manager, you will lead a team of engineers spanning quality engineering, distributed systems, and applied ML evaluation. Your team qualifies LLM inference and output-correctness automation frameworks for large-scale AI data center deployment and platform validation — validating that outputs remain correct, consistent, and stable as models, weights, prompts, serving runtimes, quantization schemes, and accelerator hardware change underneath them.
You will stay close to architecture, design reviews, and trade-offs, and partner with ML engineers, inference/performance engineers, distributed systems teams, and platform teams across Cupertino, Seattle, and other sites. You will hire and grow engineers, shape the team's roadmap, define quality bars where none exist yet, and represent the team to senior leadership and partners. This role requires strong technical depth, exceptional people-management skills, and the ability to navigate ambiguity in a fast-paced environment — including the inherently non-deterministic, probabilistic nature of generative output.
Minimum qualifications: 8+ years of experience in software and/or ML systems development, or equivalent experience.
3+ years of engineering management experience, with a proven track record of delivering complex, large-scale projects across multiple teams or organizations.
Experience architecting test, qualification, or evaluation strategy for large-scale distributed systems — ideally ML serving or inference platforms.
Hands-on background in one or more compiled languages (C, C++, Objective-C, or Swift) and proficiency in a scripting language (e.g., Python).
Self-directed: the ability to drive a strategy or project from a simple idea to production, setting clear priorities and consistently delivering on schedule with measurable outcomes.
B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with machine learning and LLMs — common practical applications and frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, or comparable inference/serving stacks).
Familiarity with LLM serving and inference optimization (batching, KV-cache, quantization, speculative decoding, distributed/multi-accelerator serving) and GPU-accelerated software.
Experience using AI/LLMs to improve testing itself — test-case generation, defect detection, or reducing manual QA effort.
Experience with CI/CD, Kubernetes, containers, and cloud-native systems, and integrating automated evals into release pipelines.

Track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong engineers, and leading change across multiple sites.

5+ years of management experience leading teams and driving delivery

title: Sr Software Engineer, Customer Systems
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization.
IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.
Customer Systems is part of IS&T and drives the technology behind Apple's customer support experience — from contact center operations to the software powering the iconic Genius Bar. The team also builds and operates AppleCare's online support platform, which handles 6 billion visits per year, delivering seamless, high-quality support to Apple customers around the globe.
Design and build microservices powering low-latency, high-throughput customer experiences — serving over a million users daily across Apple Support websites, iOS apps, and phone-based frontends.
Minimum qualifications: B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional work experience.
5+ years proven experience developing software in a professional capacity. Longer experience preferred.
2+ years proven experience with Java, including proficiency in concurrency, memory management, and performance optimization techniques.
Proficiency in OOP principles, data structures, algorithms, and software design patterns (e.g. GoF), with a proven focus on implementing testable, maintainable, and extensible backend code.
Experience building production applications with the Spring ecosystem (e.g. Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Security, Spring Data, Spring Cloud, etc.), including proficiency in dependency injection, auto-configuration, reactive programming with WebFlux, and designing microservices using Spring-based patterns.
Solid understanding of advanced JVM internals (e.g. garbage collection, memory allocation, JIT, JNI, etc.).
Experience designing, implementing, and shipping high-scale, high-performance, highly available, fault-tolerant, and secure cloud-based distributed systems.
Solid knowledge of networking concepts, protocols, and infrastructure (e.g. HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP, CDN, load balancing, edge computing, DNS, Zero Trust architecture, etc.).
Preferred qualifications: Track record of leading software projects within a team as a tech lead (TL), while mentoring software engineers.
Hands-on experience leveraging GenAI coding tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot, Codex) to accelerate the software development lifecycle, enhance code quality, and streamline debugging and testing processes.
Experience with complementary programming languages beyond Java (e.g. Go, Python, Ruby, etc.), including practical use for automation scripting, infrastructure tooling, data processing pipelines, and build system customizations.
Experience in API design and implementation, including proficiency in RESTful API principles, gRPC, GraphQL, contract-first design (e.g. OpenAPI/Swagger, Protobuf, etc.), API versioning strategies, gateway patterns, rate limiting, and designing APIs for backward compatibility and long-term evolution.
Experience with caching strategies and in-memory data technologies (e.g. Redis, Memcached, Hazelcast, Ehcache, etc.), including proficiency in cache invalidation patterns, distributed caching architectures, and session management for high-throughput applications.

title: Production Control Supervisor
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Production Control Supervisor leads our hourly warehouse, receiving, and lineside delivery teams — managing material flow across a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You'll establish and drive operational KPIs while overseeing materials from receiving and storage through kitting, line-side delivery, and shipping.

This role demands high inventory accuracy, strong safety performance, and consistent support for production teams. You won't accept the status quo — you'll identify waste, drive continuous improvement, and communicate cross-functionally to remove blockers and keep production running without interruption.

 

What You'll Do

People Leadership

 - Supervise, coach, and develop an hourly workforce — including performance feedback, conflict resolution, corrective actions, and performance improvement plans.

 - Lead by example with a strong floor presence and clear expectations for safety, quality, and productivity.

 - Monitor staffing levels, timekeeping, attendance, and shift coverage.

Warehouse & Materials Operations

 - Oversee receiving, inspection handoff, material board review, put-away, storage, picking, kitting, line-side delivery, and shipping operations.

 - Ensure material availability to production at agreed service levels while minimizing excess inventory and handling.

 - Maintain accurate inventory through disciplined cycle counts, transaction execution, and audits.

 - Enforce FIFO, shelf-life controls, and material segregation requirements.

 - Supervise internal logistics, milk runs, and material replenishment routes.

Safety, Quality & Equipment

 - Ensure compliance with company procedures and quality standards.

 - Ensure proper operation, state of charge, and maintenance of material handling equipment (forklifts, pallet jacks, ladders).

Continuous Improvement & Cost Control

 - Identify and lead process improvements to increase throughput, accuracy, and labor efficiency.

 - Drive waste reduction across space, motion, handling, and inventory.

 - Analyze operational metrics and implement corrective actions where targets are not met.

Systems & Reporting

 - Ensure accurate and timely transactions in ERP/WMS systems.

 - Track and report KPIs including inventory accuracy, on-time delivery, productivity, safety, and quality.

 - Collaborate cross-functionally with manufacturing, quality, supply chain, engineering, and logistics teams.
   
    

What You'll Bring

 - Bachelor's degree or 5+ years of experience in warehouse, materials, manufacturing, or supply chain operations.

 - 1+ year of experience leading or supervising hourly teams in an operational environment.

 - Strong understanding of inventory control, material flow, and production support.

 - Experience with ERP/WMS systems (Odoo, SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar).

 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office with advanced Excel skills.

 - Ability to operate material handling equipment including forklifts; able to lift up to 75 lbs and work at heights with or without accommodation.

 - Willingness to work extended hours, weekends, or alternate shifts as required.

 

About the Team

The Production Control team exists to ensure every part, kit, and shipment is exactly where it needs to be — at the right time, in the right quantity, and in the right condition — so production can move without interruption. Our work directly enables Base to build and deploy reliable energy systems by creating a materials operation that is accurate, disciplined, and built for scale. The challenges we solve are tangible and high-impact: preventing line stoppages, protecting inventory integrity, and designing material flow that can keep up with rapid growth.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

title: Product Manager - Chicago, IL
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role:
As a Product Manager at MISUMI Americas, you will own a defined product area — whether a feature set, a workflow, a capability, or a segment of our platform — and be responsible for delivering strong, well-executed product work within it. You will gather and synthesize customer, stakeholder, and performance insights; write clear requirements; partner closely with Engineering and Design on delivery; and track outcomes to drive continuous improvement.
This role is designed for someone who is serious about the craft of product management and is ready to build the depth of judgment and business understanding needed to take on broader ownership over time. You will be expected to deliver reliably, communicate clearly, build credibility with your cross-functional partners, and show increasing independence as you develop fluency in the domain. The best PMs in this role will grow into Senior PMs who own full product areas with strategic autonomy.
You will report to the VP, Product Management.
Areas of Responsibility:
Business acumen and domain awareness
Develop a deep understanding of the customers, internal users, and business context relevant to your product area — including how your work connects to broader platform goals and company priorities
Research and synthesize customer needs, stakeholder feedback, and operational realities to build a clear, grounded point of view on the problems your team should be solving
Assess the needs of internal users across Operations, Sales, and other functions, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and remove friction in workflows that touch your area
Stay current on how your product area is performing — tracking metrics, monitoring trends, and developing hypotheses about where the biggest opportunities for improvement lie
Build familiarity with the competitive landscape and with how MISUMI Americas' platform capabilities compare to alternatives available to our customers
Roadmap contribution, work analysis, and scoping
Contribute to roadmap development within your area with increasing independence, translating high-level goals into clearly scoped objectives, projects, and requirements
Develop and maintain a framework for tracking input and output metrics that provide a quantitative view of the success and impact of your work
Build business cases for prioritized initiatives, articulating the customer value, business rationale, and expected outcomes in a way that earns stakeholder confidence
Scope and define requirements for roadmap items with clarity and specificity — ensuring Engineering and Design have what they need to build the right thing, efficiently
Proactively identify trade-offs and risks associated with scope and sequencing decisions, and work collaboratively with your team to develop pragmatic mitigation approaches
Establish and communicate a well-reasoned point of view on the problems your team should prioritize and why
Cross-functional collaboration
Build strong working relationships with Engineering, Design, Operations, Sales, and other functions — earning trust through clear communication, good judgment, and consistent follow-through
Lead cross-functional meetings within your area to align on scope, priorities, and requirements — ensuring that all relevant perspectives are heard and decisions are made with shared understanding
Actively seek feedback from stakeholders and adjust plans accordingly, fostering a responsive and collaborative approach to product development
Work with cross-functional partners to develop and evaluate hypotheses about customer needs and solutions, bringing both rigor and creativity to discovery
Communicate team progress and results to stakeholders with transparency — celebrating wins and ensuring the organization learns from setbacks
Execution and risk management
Apply Agile methodologies to organize and manage sprints, supporting a streamlined and efficient development process within your team
Partner closely with Engineering to estimate scope and timelines, continuously refining plans as work progresses and new information emerges
Keep stakeholders informed of project status, proactively flagging risks or deviations from plan and proposing solutions rather than just surfacing problems
Drive product launches by ensuring that all relevant parts of the organization — Engineering, Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Support — are prepared and aligned
Analyze metrics post-launch to evaluate impact, identify gaps, and inform the next iteration of your roadmap
Travel up to 10% annually for team collaboration, customer research, and training
Desired Traits and Qualifications, Education and Experience Equivalency:
Past Experience:
2–4 years of product management experience, ideally in a B2B software, e-commerce, or platform environment
Demonstrated experience owning a defined product area from discovery through delivery — including writing requirements, managing scope, and tracking outcomes
Experience working closely with Engineering and Design teams in an Agile development environment
Track record of building productive working relationships with cross-functional stakeholders and earning credibility through clear communication and reliable execution
Experience using data and customer insights to inform prioritization decisions and evaluate the impact of product changes
Familiarity with defining and tracking product metrics — both leading indicators and business outcomes
Desired
Experience in one or more of the following domains: catalog and search, e-commerce platform, supply chain or order management, customer experience, or internal business systems
Exposure to platforms with large or complex catalogs, configurable products, or high-SKU-count inventory — where search relevance, attribute structure, and navigation design are meaningful product challenges
Familiarity with industrial manufacturing, hardware product development, or engineering procurement workflows — or a genuine interest in developing that knowledge quickly
Experience with operational tooling or business systems (e.g., ERP, CMS, CRM, PIM) and how they interact with customer-facing product experiences
Skills
Strong analytical skills: able to break high-level goals into actionable requirements by synthesizing data, customer insights, and stakeholder input to drive sound product decisions
Clear written and verbal communication: able to write crisp requirements and PRDs, facilitate productive cross-functional discussions, and give stakeholders the information they need to act
Structured thinking: approaches ambiguous problems with a clear process — defining the problem, gathering evidence, framing options, and making a reasoned recommendation
Results orientation: focused on outcomes and impact, not just completing tasks — takes ownership of the success of their work end to end
Collaborative working style: builds relationships across functions with empathy and accountability, and earns credibility through consistency and follow-through
Active and growing AI practice: uses AI tools as a genuine accelerant for drafting, research synthesis, and ideation — and demonstrates intellectual curiosity and learning velocity in developing new AI-assisted workflows as the tooling landscape evolves
Builder mindset: comfortable experimenting with AI-assisted prototyping to communicate product ideas, test assumptions, and accelerate the feedback loop — treating working artifacts as a complement to written documentation, not a replacement for it
Curiosity and learning agility: proactively seeks to understand the business, the customer, and the technical context — and applies new knowledge to improve their product decisions

Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!

Partner with cross-functional teams: IT, Legal, connected product, and business units to embed security best practices and continuously improve the maturity, efficiency, and clarity of processes and reporting.

Demonstrated experience owning cybersecurity governance, risk, or compliance programs and producing executive- or board-level reporting.
Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST CSF and CMMC, and of enterprise risk and third-party risk management practices.
Experience coordinating security awareness, data security, or identity governance programs across cross-functional stakeholders.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for technical and non-technical audiences, including leadership.
Strong analytical, organizational, and program-management skills.

Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, or CompTIA Security+.
Experience with GRC and risk platforms and data security tooling.

title: Director Enterprise Learning
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The opportunity:
Advancing minimally invasive care requires more than great technology — it requires people who grow with the company, lead with intention, and bring their best to every challenge. The Director, Enterprise Learning will shape how we build capability from the inside out: ensuring every employee, manager, and director has the knowledge, skills, and mindset to perform and grow.
We're looking for someone who sees learning as a business discipline, not a support function. Someone who starts with strategy — understanding where Intuitive is headed and what capabilities will get us there — and works backward to design learning that actually moves the needle. A builder who combines learning design expertise with sharp business judgment, and who knows how to measure whether any of it is working.
This role covers role agnostic enterprise learning below the VP level: individual contributor development, manager learning, director learning, and employee onboarding. It's a broad remit that requires both vision and execution — and a leader who can do both.
What you'll lead:
You'll report directly to the VP, Global Talent and own the strategy, design, and delivery of enterprise-wide learning programs that are connected to business priorities, deliver measurable impact, and built to last. This isn't about building a curriculum library — it's about building capability that shows up in business results.
What this looks like:
Anchor learning to business strategy. Partner closely with HR Business Partners, business leaders, and the broader Talent team to understand where the company is going and what capabilities will be required to get there. Translate that into a multi-year enterprise learning strategy with clear priorities, measurable outcomes, and a coherent point of view on what we build, buy, or curate.
Design learning that works. Lead the design and delivery of learning experiences across the full employee population — from onboarding through director-level development. Apply modern instructional design principles across a range of modalities: in-person, digital, cohort-based, on-demand, and AI-enabled. Prioritize approaches that fit how people actually learn at work.
Own manager and director development. Build and continuously evolve learning programs for managers and directors that are practical, relevant, and grounded in what Intuitive needs from its people leaders. Work closely with HR Business Partners to ensure programs address real capability gaps, not just generic leadership topics.
Deliver a best-in-class onboarding experience. Design and steward an onboarding experience that accelerates time-to-productivity, connects new employees to Intuitive's mission and culture, and sets a strong foundation for long-term engagement and performance.
Make learning measurable. Define clear success metrics for every major program and build the infrastructure to track them. Move beyond attendance and satisfaction scores — connect learning outcomes to performance, retention, and business impact. Use data to make honest calls about what's working and what isn't.
Bring modern learning approaches to life. Stay close to how the learning landscape is evolving — AI-enabled personalization, digital learning platforms, cohort learning, nudge-based reinforcement — and bring the right innovations into Intuitive in ways that are practical and scalable, not just novel.
Build and lead a high-performing team. Lead a team of learning professionals with clarity, high standards, and genuine investment in their development. Create an environment where craft matters, outcomes are tracked, and continuous improvement is the norm.

title: Senior Program Manager, People Experience & Operations
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Senior Program Manager, People Experience & Operations is a trusted partner to the Vice President of PXO and a key integrator across People Services, People Technology & Digital Employee Experience, and People Analytics. This role combines the judgment and executive partnership of a chief of staff with the discipline of a portfolio program manager and the ownership of a hands-on operator.
Working through program and project managers across the broader HR organization, this person builds a cohesive view of the most important work: what is underway, how initiatives connect, where decisions or resources are needed, and what could put delivery at risk. They establish clear operating rhythms and scalable ways of working, while directly leading select cross-functional priorities. The role is not intended to replace the PMs accountable for individual projects. It makes their work easier to connect, prioritize, and communicate at a leadership level.
Key Responsibilities
Portfolio Integration, Visibility & Governance
·   Partner with PMs, functional leaders, and the broader HR PMO to consolidate existing project plans and updates into a decision-ready view of the PXO portfolio, without duplicating project-level ownership or reporting.
·   Map dependencies, milestones, decisions, risks, resource constraints, and ownership across initiatives; identify collisions or sequencing issues early and drive the right conversations to resolve them.
·   Establish lightweight standards and practical routines for intake, portfolio reviews, escalation, decision logs, and follow-through; improve data quality and accountability without creating unnecessary process.
·   Translate portfolio information into concise executive dashboards and narratives that distinguish what is on track, what needs attention, and where VP or leadership intervention will make a difference.
Executive Partnership & Operating Rhythm
·   Serve as a trusted thought partner to the VP, connecting the dots across teams, anticipating needs, pressure-testing options, and translating priorities into clear next steps.
·   Run an effective leadership operating cadence: staff meetings, agendas, pre-reads, decision tracking, quarterly priorities, leadership offsites, and follow-up on commitments.
·   Develop clear, audience-appropriate briefings, presentations, communications, and recommendations for senior HR, IT, Finance, and other stakeholders.
·   Support planning and prioritization by bringing visibility to commitments, capacity, headcount and budget dependencies, and trade-offs; partner with accountable functional and Finance leaders rather than assuming their ownership.
Complex Programs & Special Initiatives
·   Personally lead selected high-priority initiatives that span teams or lack a natural owner, from framing the problem and aligning stakeholders through execution and measurable outcomes.
·   Build practical plans, clarify decision rights, surface blockers with recommendations, and drive action across matrixed partners without relying on formal authority.
·   Help leaders navigate change, coordinate communications and handoffs, and turn ambiguous or fast-moving requirements into repeatable, scalable approaches.
Employee Experience, Connection & Communication
·   Help shape and deliver purposeful PXO all-hands, team forums, recognition practices, and leadership events that strengthen connection across a global organization.
·   Partner with leaders to turn employee survey and listening insights into meaningful actions, track commitments, and close the feedback loop.
·   Bring care and consistency to team communications and operating rituals so people feel informed, recognized, and connected to the broader purpose of the work.
What You Bring
·   8+ years of experience in complex program or portfolio management, business operations, enterprise transformation, or a chief of staff–type role, with evidence of outcomes across functions.
·   Experience working with multiple project or program managers to synthesize a portfolio view, navigate cross-project dependencies, and support executive decisions. You can see the system without losing the details.
·   Excellent judgment, discretion, and executive communication: you simplify complexity, bring options rather than just problems, and know when to act independently or escalate.
·   A builder mindset. You create structure where it is missing, improve processes without adding bureaucracy, and turn ambiguous needs into practical solutions that last.
·   Exceptional follow-through, organization, and ownership, paired with curiosity, humility, empathy, a positive and collaborative approach, and an instinct for bringing people together.
·   Confidence influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority, handling confidential information responsibly, and staying composed when priorities shift.
·   An AI-forward or AI-curious mindset: you proactively explore appropriate AI and automation tools to improve synthesis, reporting, workflows, and productivity, while exercising strong judgment about accuracy, privacy, and data security.
·   Proficiency in presentation, spreadsheet, collaboration, and project/portfolio management tools; bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Experience
·   Experience in People/HR functions, HR technology, enterprise services, or a global matrixed or regulated business.
·   Familiarity with platforms such as Workday, ServiceNow, Qualtrics, Smartsheet, or equivalent tools, as well as change management or employee listening programs.
·   Experience supporting VP-level leadership, including operating reviews, executive communications, and cross-functional annual planning; relevant PMP training is a plus.
What Success Looks Like
The VP and PXO leadership have a clear, trusted view of the portfolio and can quickly see key dependencies, trade-offs, owners, risks, and decisions. PMs across HR have a collaborative partner who connects their work rather than recreating it. Important initiatives move forward, commitments are followed through, and the team benefits from clear communication, thoughtful recognition, and consistent operating practices. Above all, this person is known for sound judgment, initiative, reliability, and making both leaders and colleagues more effective.

Primary Function of Position:
The Senior Financial Analyst will serve as a strategic business partner to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Organization, with a focus on Global Access, Value, & Economics (GAVE) and Comparative Medicine team, supporting budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, business analytics, and executive decision support. The role will translate complex financial and operational data into actionable insights that support strategic priorities and informed decision-making. This position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of finance, business planning, analytics, and executive decision support within a fast-growing healthcare technology organization.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Financial Planning and Analysis
Prepare and coordinate the annual budget, quarterly forecasts, and long-range planning process for GAVE and Comparative Medicine.
Analyze operating expenses, variances, and business drivers to identify risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Conduct month-end close activities in partnership with Accounting team.

Business Partnership and Decision Support
Build trusted partnerships with GAVE and Comparative Medicine leaders and provide proactive financial guidance on business priorities, investments, risks, and opportunities.
Prepare financial analyses and presentations that translate complex information into clear recommendations.
Provide timely financial analysis and decision support for emerging business priorities.
Analytics and Business Performance
Develop and maintain business performance dashboards, KPI frameworks, and management reporting packages.
Perform benchmarking and analyze financial and operational performance to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
Identify and implement process improvements through standardization and automation to streamline recurring activities.
Required Skills and Experience
Minimum 5 years of relevant finance or accounting experience, including budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with the ability to deliver accurate analyses and translate complex data into actionable business insights.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with executive leadership.
Proven self-starter with the ability to work effectively in a cross-functional, fast-paced environment.
Highly organized, with the ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects concurrently.
High degree of ownership, intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and attention to detail.
This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week
Required Education and Training
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, data analytics, or a related field.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in Tableau.
Proficiency in writing SQL queries preferred.
