If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient safety as our highest priority.
Primary Function of Position:
The mission of Supplier Engineering is to ensure high quality and stable delivery of purchased production components from suppliers operating under robust quality systems. Each supplier engineer is responsible for ensuring suppliers meet ISI requirements for product quality, cost, and service.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Part Qualification
Lead Part Qualification activities in support of NPI programs
Lead Core Product Teams in defining appropriate Part Qualification requirements This includes defining testing and inspection requirements prior to system integration in order to maximize ISI factory efficiency
Support transfer of parts and suppliers to production
Complete Production Part Qualification Process deliverables: Supplier pFMEA, Special Process Validations, FAI, and Process Capability Analysis Perform product/process risk analysis and ensure mitigations are implemented and effective prior to product introduction
Establish sustainable process capability at supplier and critical sub-tier suppliers
Lead Commodity/Supplier level corrections
Drive corrective actions through use of various Root Cause tools (8D, 5 Why, etc), determining true root cause, implementing effective and lasting corrective and preventive actions
Manufacturing Process Selection and Development
Lead manufacturing process selection
Identify the correct process for manufacturing the part, considering process quality, long term capacity and total lifecycle cost.
Identify where DFM is appropriate to achieve higher quality, lower costs or better supply chain capacity
Educate internal customers and suppliers regarding supplier quality, process and operational capabilities, best value manufacturing methods and tooling for key supplier processes
Manage change
Drive improvements to ISI requirements as necessary by proposing and managing changes to specifications and drawings through the ECO process
Manage the planning and implementation of supplier change management projects using the Supplier Change Request process (SCR) post Design V&V
Provide status of the readiness (quality, capacity, delivery) of the supply chain for major production process changes
Work cross-functionally to improve supplier engineering processes
Supplier Selection and Evaluation
Support Supplier Selection
Work with Product Design, Commodity Mangers and other stake holders to identify high capability suppliers necessary for New Products based on assessment of business need and supplier capability.
Evaluate new supplies through informal assessments and formal assessment by supporting lead auditors in QMS evaluations
Foster Supplier Relationships
Support audit team in addressing findings to develop suppliers’ quality and business systems in order to meet ISI’s requirements
Manage supplier relationships to effectively collaborate with Intuitive

In order to adequately perform the responsibilities of this position the individual must possess:
BS degree in Engineering field
10+ years related experience in Manufacturing, Supplier Process Engineering, Design, or related field
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience creating and aggregating DFM feedback
Demonstrable knowledge in evaluating and challenging supplier technical, quality, and business capabilities
Experience with a wide range of manufacturing processes including understanding of key input variables for quality, cost and capacity Desired product experience in at least one of the following categories: Mechanical Motion Products (Bearings, Gears and Screws)
Mechanical Motion Control Products (Motors, Brakes)
Motion Control Electronics (Encoders, Inertial Sensors, Resolvers)
Proven ability to motivate suppliers and lead teams to solve difficult technical and process problems
Knowledge of pFMEA, process validation, inspection and test techniques
Familiarity with 21 CFR part 820 and ISO 13485 Experience in auditing suppliers to these standards is preferred
At a minimum, candidate should understand GDP and QMS methods
Significant computer experience using Windows, Word, Excel, Access and ERP Information Systems, preferably SAP
Ability to read and interpret detailed specifications and schematics and communicate technical information
Experience in a medical device company is a preferred
Experience with low-volume high-mix production environments is preferred
Ability to travel to suppliers on an as needed basis – domestic and international

title: da Vinci Specialist
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion—have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you’ll find your purpose here.
*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to the St. Louis  Area to perform the duties of this role.
Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

title: Director, Internal Controls
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Position Overview
The Director of Internal Controls will build and lead a practical, business-focused enterprise internal control and risk management program that supports Invenergy’s continued growth. This role will partner directly with leaders across finance, accounting, technology, legal, compliance, development, construction, and operations to identify and assess significant risks, establish scalable controls, strengthen process documentation, and promote clear ownership and accountability.
The Director will be a hands-on leader who can set the strategy, develop the program, and work alongside the business to provide practical, risk-based guidance and maintain an effective, sustainable control environment as the organization evolves.
Responsibilities
Build and lead a formal annual enterprise risk assessment process that identifies significant risks across the organization, evaluates their relative likelihood and impact, and maps the controls intended to mitigate those risks.
Incorporate fraud risk into the annual assessment, including potential fraud schemes, incentives and opportunities, management override, and the preventive and detective controls needed to address those risks.
Maintain a practical, formally documented risk and internal control inventory that identifies each objective, associated risk, control activity, owner, and frequency, and ensure it is updated as the business, systems, risks, and processes change.
Ensure key processes and controls are supported by approved, usable procedures that define the control objective, execution steps, frequency, preparer, reviewer, exception handling, escalation, and required evidence.
Develop a scalable internal control framework and operating model that reflects Invenergy’s ownership structure, business complexity, growth plans, and risk profile.
Work directly with business and functional leaders to establish clear accountability and design controls that are effective, efficient, and integrated into day-to-day operations.
Perform and oversee periodic reviews of control design and operation, identify gaps, agree on practical corrective actions with management, and monitor remediation through completion.
Challenge existing processes constructively and identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and strengthen controls while supporting speed, accountability, and business growth.
Establish and maintain formal internal audit procedures, including a risk-based annual audit plan, scoping, planning, fieldwork, sampling, testing, documentation, quality review, reporting, issue rating, management responses, remediation follow-up, and escalation.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity for internal audit activities and coordinate efficiently with external auditors, legal, compliance, technology, and other assurance partners.
Provide concise, decision-useful reporting to senior management and other governance stakeholders on key risks, control coverage, audit results, open issues, remediation progress, and emerging concerns.

We’re looking for passionate talent who dare to dream big, agile collaborators who talk straight and decide fast, and driven performers with a growth mindset. If this inspires and energizes you, you’ve found the right place where you can do cool things with fun people for one of the biggest snacking companies in the world!
The Opportunity: Why This Role Matters
This is a project-based, 24-month assignment for a food safety expert who thrives on driving change and innovation. We're looking for a specialist to lead critical laboratory and technology programs aimed at making our products safer, optimizing our processes, and reducing verification costs. In this role, you will be the bridge between cutting-edge technology and our manufacturing reality, taking new analytical methods from the lab bench and deploying them in the field. You'll also partner directly with our Supply Quality Assurance (SQA) team, acting as a microbiological expert for high-risk ingredient suppliers and serving as the authorized witness for critical food safety dispositions. This is your chance to make a significant, measurable impact on how we ensure quality across the Accelerator division.
What You’ll Do (Key Responsibilities)
Lead Laboratory & Technology Programs:   Manage the network of third-party labs, optimize testing practices, and serve as the SME for internal laboratories. Validate and deploy new food safety technologies and analytical methods (e.g., CleanWorks, Gene-UP).
Drive Supplier Quality:   Provide microbiological expertise and support SQA during audits of high-risk supplier manufacturing sites. Partner with SQA on Material Risk Assessments (MRA), ingredient specifications, and Inbound Verification Testing (IVT).
Manage Quality Incidents & Risk:   Provide PRIMP support by managing escalated testing and leading laboratory investigations. Support the division's quality risk management activities, ensuring risks are documented and tracked in the Archer platform.
Oversee Data & Training:   Oversee the trending of finished product test data, leading quarterly reviews to provide recommendations for optimization. Develop and deliver training to build food safety and laboratory capability among internal teams.
Act as Authorized Witness:   Serve as the authorized witness for the disposition of food safety-critical materials, ensuring compliance with Mars corporate standards.
What We’re Looking For
A Lab & Technology Expert:   Advanced knowledge of microbiological and allergen hazards, analytical methods, and laboratory quality systems (e.g., ISO 17025).
A Project-Driven Doer:   Proven experience managing projects, from pilot trials and data validation to the full deployment of new technologies in a manufacturing environment.
A Supplier Quality Partner:   Experience auditing operational processes, particularly for high-risk ingredient suppliers, and a strong understanding of MRAs and IVT.
An Independent Collaborator:   The ability to work with a high degree of autonomy while building strong relationships with SQA, R&D, and external lab partners to get things done.
Qualifications
Education:   Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Biology, or a closely related field.
Experience:   7+ years of experience in food manufacturing and laboratory quality systems.
Certifications:   HACCP or related certification required. Certification and experience auditing operational processes required.
Location:   Based in Chicago, IL or Battle Creek, MI.
Travel:   Ability to travel (~30%) to labs and manufacturing sites.

title: Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview
As a  Critical Environment Technician (CET)  in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will help to maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our datacenters up and running. This could be anything from performing basic monitoring and inspection, performing various types of maintenance, participating in equipment troubleshooting, enforcing all safety and security requirements, and developing methods of operating procedures (MOPs) and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for appropriately leveled procedures to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments.
Develops an understanding of method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs lower level maintenance with minimal supervision, and may resolve high level issues with support from more experienced colleagues. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safely responds to and stabilizes abnormal conditions within the required timeframes for various abnormal facility events within data center with minimal supervision, utilizing emergency operating procedures (EOPs). Gathers necessary information and participates in the creation of incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Assists in developing emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Assists in providing emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Works on tasks (e.g., making rounds, initial assessments on equipment performance) as assigned with varying levels of supervision, sometime minimal. Supports senior colleagues as an assistant. Builds knowledge in operating equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls). Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Performs monitoring physical inspection of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify critical alarms. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems.
Physical Requirements Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
As indicated above,   have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Other
Embodies our  culture  and  values .
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 1+ year(s) technical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical)

Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Appropriately takes action and reports physical security access concerns and/or incidents to direct-line management or established reporting methods.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

Escalates and/or seeks guidance from experienced technicians or direct-line management regarding client interactions.

This role brings together product design, interaction design, animation, AI, storytelling, and software development. You will explore emerging technologies, experiment with new forms of human–AI interaction, and develop prototypes, tools, and reusable systems that help move ideas from early exploration toward real product experiences.
The ideal candidate is as comfortable imagining new product possibilities and crafting intuitive, expressive experiences as writing code, connecting systems, and debugging prototypes. You should bring deep expertise in at least one discipline and a demonstrated ability to bridge creative thinking and technical execution.
The future of Copilot and AI must be experienced, not just imagined. From entirely new product ideas, features, and interactions to embodied AI characters and how they move, speak, behave, and respond, the most compelling possibilities come to life through tangible, interactive experiences that people can see, feel, and explore.
You will help build the Creative Studio’s ability to imagine, prototype, validate, and bring these ideas to life—connecting creative strategy, design, storytelling, and emerging technologies to new product possibilities, strengthening shared technical capabilities, and bridging the gap between creative vision and implementation.

Develop and prototype future AI experiences. Translate blue-sky Copilot and AI product ideas, narratives, and creative concepts into compelling UI explorations, UX flows, interactive demos, and working prototypes that advance the product experience, brand, identity, and creative vision.

Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across Creative, Research, Product, and Engineering to develop, evaluate, and advance ideas from early exploration toward implementation.

title: Senior Critical Environment Technician (Night Shift)
description:
Overview
As a Senior Critical Environment Technician (CET) in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, working closely with Management to address operational, risk and safety situations, mentoring other CE Technicians, having a hands-on understanding on how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Performs troubleshooting of equipment and systems independently within their trained discipline(s). Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Communicates and/or escalates troubleshooting issues or anomalies with assistance from more experienced colleagues. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs (e.g., basic replacements, changing of parts) for specific disciplines and equipment for which they have been trained, following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. As a CO+I Senior Logistics Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.   Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.   With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.   Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.   In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.    Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Customer Service
Maintains a strong focus to understand the impact of their work when completing tickets and assigned Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) tasks. Communicates across Data Center teams (e.g., Site Services, Critical Environment, Facility Management, Security, Vendors, Safety, Supply Chain), and supports Microsoft and non-Microsoft gear deliveries. Ensures IAM tasks are completed accurately as requested, as well as meet company and industry standards and policies. Builds strong working relationships with customers. Identifies, coordinates, manages expectations, and offers alternatives when defining stakeholder solutions in light of ongoing company standards, operations, and procedures (e.g., schedule, technical feasibility, policy, procedure, tools).
Data Bearing Device (DBD) Destruction
Performs destruction of data bearing devices (DBD) following all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Microsoft policies as necessary. Ensures DBD serial number matches with database. Coordinates with and oversees any third-party vendors who perform DBD destruction as necessary. Begins to act as a resource for the decommissioning process to ensure customer security is maintained, performing data bearing devices (DBD) destruction as necessary. Decommissions servers, maintaining compliance, meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and documenting actions taken against a decommissioning workflow.
Fleet Management
Performs weekly vehicle inspections. Coordinates with other teams (e.g., IT, CE) on location of equipment and staging on docs.
Inbound and Outbound Logistics
Coordinates, prepares, and executes incoming/outgoing deliveries (e.g. purchase order [PO] receiving, Rack Movement Supervisor [RMS] activities) based on site-class designation. Documents inbound/outbound packages. Receives, confirms, tracks, stores, dispatches, and delivers material from the warehouse to destinations, including production facilities, retail stores, and corporate offices. Begins to communicate directly with customers, stakeholders, vendors, (e.g., landlords) in regard to scheduling both inbound and outbound deliveries. Applies appropriate customs documentations and standards for outbound packages. Ensures complete and detailed physical inventory tracking and staging.
IT Inventory Management
Maintains and stewards up-to-date and accurate logical information within various inventory management systems (e.g., configuration management databases, asset management repositories). Performs inventory cycle audits, data corrections, and various Data Center regulatory compliance or certification control audit activity. Performs material movement, including shipping/receiving and inventory management per standard process. Starts to monitor and prioritize ticketing queues, works to resolve escalations, and clears blocking issues to enable continued delivery of Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) activities.
Operational Excellence
Follows procedures to contribute to plans to develop, build, and run methodologies. Ensures execution according to accepted procedures for consistency, accuracy, and timeliness of delivery. Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies. Complies with environmental sustainability and zero waste initiatives. Facilitates training for relevant site-specific procedures and tools (e.g., forklift, pallet jacks, technician on-hand processes, inventory maintenance software, RMA portals, Rack Movement).
Procurement
Notifies management about ordering stock shortages. Escalates any issues to management.
Safety Practices
Complies with security and data management policies. Escalates any security or safety incidents. Coordinates with security escorts for third-party vendors. Engages in Task Hazard Analysis (THA) consistently for every task to be performed and ensures sign off from appropriate person for any related risks. Conducts rack movement activities, supporting training on devices and tools and upholding safety standards. Follows established protocols on dealing with unsafe materials out of containment, leveraging safety alert system, escalating to management, and properly disposing of them.
Tactical Shift Management
Ensures plans to maintain and organize space are followed. Performs assigned tasks and escalates issues during high-volume work activity or escalation-based situations. Leverages process knowledge and best judgment to complete next task without direct supervision. Monitors inbound and outbound schedules, escalating deviations from scheduling. Receives and organizes deliveries for supported groups (e.g., IT, Critical Environments, Facility Management, third-party supplies, etc.)
Travel and Work Hours
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday. Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Warranty Process Management
Engages supplier to initiate warranty claim when automation is not available and processes the orders. Processes failed vendor hardware devices using online/other tools, including information processing, packaging, shipment, and receipt of return for Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) and non-RMA devices. Performs manual return processes for non-RMA failed parts. Begins to perform manual ordering processes of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. Follows all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) related to RMA and non-RMA warranty process.

Required/minimum qualifications
High School Diploma AND 1+ years experience in warehouse/supply chain in an information technology (IT) environment, logistics, supply chain, inventory management, retail, or a related field OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Additional or preferred qualifications
2+ years experience in warehouse/supply chain in an information technology (IT) environment, logistics, supply chain, inventory management, retail, or a related field OR equivalent experience.

title: Software Engineer II & Senior Software Engineer - (CoreAI Speech, Translation, and Data Platforms)
description:
Overview
The Microsoft CoreAI Speech and Languages Teams are building speech and language technologies and data foundations that power the next generation of AI experiences. We are hiring software engineers for opportunities across three teams: Speech Service and Runtime, Speech and Language Translation, and Data Processing for Speech. We are looking for both Software Engineer II and Senior Software Engineers.
You will design, build, and optimize software that brings speech and AI technologies into production. Depending on the team, your work will focus on real-time speech recognition engines and cloud services, speech and language translation solutions, or an agentic data processing platform for speech and AI model development.
Our speech technologies support scenarios such as meeting transcription and summarization, agent commanding, dictation, and task completion, powering Teams, M365 Copilot, Voice Agent, Windows, and other first- and third-party experiences. Our data platform supports the end-to-end data lifecycle, including data acquisition and generation, processing, filtering, quality validation, and data preparation across speech, audio, text, and other machine learning data.
You will collaborate with engineers, applied scientists, researchers, customer-facing teams, and partner teams to translate customer, engineering, and research needs into scalable, reliable software. These opportunities span distributed systems, cloud services, speech, translation, data engineering, and AI, with the technical focus varying by team.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Join a culture that values growth mindset, diverse perspectives, continuous learning, and thoughtful engineering collaboration.
Responsibilities
Across these teams, you will:
Design, implement, test, and deliver production-quality software, contributing from requirements and technical design through cloud deployment and ongoing operation.
Build scalable, reliable systems and optimize performance across software components, AI models, distributed compute, and cloud infrastructure.
Collaborate with engineers, modeling experts, researchers, and partner teams to architect end-to-end solutions and respond to evolving customer and research needs.
Maintain high standards for code quality, testing, debugging, reliability, and operational excellence, and contribute through design discussions and code reviews.
Develop cloud services and secure execution environments that support AI agents, workflow orchestration, and tool integration.
Depending on your team, your responsibilities will include:
Speech Service and Runtime: Develop robust speech recognition software across scenarios, languages, and compute platforms; design and optimize high-performance components and algorithms for real-time recognition engines and services.
Speech and Language Translation: Build and optimize speech and language translation software, engines, and services, collaborating with modeling and partner teams to deliver end-to-end solutions.
Data Processing for Speech: Design, build, and evolve an agentic data processing platform using Python, Apache Spark/PySpark, and Microsoft Azure. Develop capabilities for data acquisition and generation, processing, filtering, quality validation, and preparation; build tools, abstractions, workflow automation, and AI-powered capabilities that improve scalability, reliability, efficiency, and developer productivity.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, Python, C#, C++, or Java OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements is required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to, the following specialized security screening: Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Qualifications:
Relevant experience in one or more of the following areas is preferred; the technical focus varies by team:
Proven programming, algorithm design, and software engineering skills, including design, implementation, testing, debugging, and delivery of high-quality production software using Python, C#, C++, Java, Rust, or another modern programming language.
Experience with speech recognition, speech and language translation, AI/ML systems, or speech, audio, text, and other machine learning data.
Experience optimizing performance for recognition engines, real-time services, or AI/ML systems, including work with GPU computing, CUDA, or PyTorch.
Experience with Apache Spark/PySpark, Databricks, or similar distributed data processing platforms.
Experience with distributed systems, data engineering, production data pipelines, workflow orchestration, or large-scale data platforms.
Experience designing and developing cloud-based services, systems, or data platforms on Microsoft Azure or comparable cloud platforms, including containerized services or secure execution environments.
Experience with large language models, agents, agentic workflows, agent runtimes, tool integration, or agent-driven development.
Proven problem-solving and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to work across software, data, infrastructure, and AI components.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, effective collaboration, and the ability to think independently, build support for ideas, and translate them into technical results.
Master’s degree or higher in computer science, mathematics, or engineering.

title: Researcher, Frontier Robustness
description:
About the Team

The Frontier Robustness team advances the science of securing frontier AI systems. We develop new methods to keep increasingly capable models contained, observable, and under human control, focusing on the sandboxes, shared research infrastructure, and protective systems used during model development and evaluation.

We use our most capable models to discover and combine weaknesses across the security stack, studying how they might escape containment, communicate through unauthorized channels, or evade monitoring. We turn these findings into new defenses and test whether protections hold as models, environments, and attack strategies change.



About the Role

We are looking for a researcher to develop and test new methods for securing frontier AI systems. You will investigate open-ended questions about model behavior, containment, and safeguards—designing experiments, building evaluations, and developing defenses where established approaches may be insufficient. You will work closely with the Security organization to define the problems and translate research findings into practical protections.

You will take research from an initial question and threat model through experiment design, reproducible findings, and tested defenses. You will write code, build tools and prototypes, and work closely with researchers and infrastructure owners to turn new ideas into safeguards that work in practice. This requires sound security judgment, comfort with uncertainty, and the ability to devise solutions to problems without established answers. This role is based in San Francisco.



In this role, you will:

 - Design and run experiments using frontier models and hands-on security techniques to discover failure modes in sandboxes, research infrastructure, and the services models can reach. Reproduce vulnerabilities and assess their impact.

 - Develop threat models and novel adversarial tests for attacks that cross multiple security boundaries, including sandbox escapes, unauthorized communication between agents, and access to sensitive data or systems through shared services.

 - Invent, prototype, and evaluate defenses that strengthen isolation and limit the impact of a compromised boundary. Study agent permissions and tool configurations to identify excessive access and build layered protections with infrastructure owners.

 - Develop and red-team model-based safeguards and monitors of model reasoning and actions. Investigate evasion, test new monitoring techniques, and measure when protections detect or prevent unsafe behavior.

 - Develop automated adversarial tests and repeatable evaluations to measure progress as model capabilities, configurations, and attack strategies change. Assess whether defenses generalize to new attacks, verify fixes, and identify regressions.

 - Partner across Research, Security, and infrastructure teams, including Agent Security, to prioritize risks and turn findings into deployed improvements while accounting for performance and researcher workflows.
   
   

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on experience conducting research with large language models, including designing and running experiments and evaluating model behavior.

 - Can turn an open-ended question into a clear hypothesis, build reproducible experiments at scale, and use the results to develop or improve a method.

 - Can design rigorous evaluations, investigate unexpected results, and test whether findings hold across different models, environments, and attack strategies.

 - Write and debug code independently, build research tools and prototypes, and carry ideas through experimentation.

 - Bring practical security experience relevant to this work, such as sandboxing, vulnerability research, adversarial testing, or detection and monitoring.

title: Director of Facilities
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Director of Facilities
The Director of Facilities will have end-to-end accountability for the operational performance, physical condition, safety, functionality, and employee experience of Quince's headquarters in both San Francisco and Palo Alto.  This is a hands-on role that will require on-location presence in both locations weekly.
A defining responsibility of this position will be helping Quince transition into a significantly larger, more complex headquarters building in San Francisco. The Director will partner with internal leadership, the relocation project manager, architects, contractors, and service providers to ensure the new headquarters is fully operational, exceptionally maintained, and equipped to support the company's continued growth.  The role will
Following the relocation, this leader will oversee all aspects of headquarters facilities operations, including building systems, maintenance, workplace services, security coordination, vendor management, budgets, sample and fabric library operations, and ongoing improvements.
The Director will also lead a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, ensuring product samples and fabric materials are accurately tracked, organized, maintained, and readily accessible to Quince's merchandising, product development, design, and other internal teams.
Responsibilities
1. New Headquarters Relocation & Operational Readiness
Play a central leadership role in Quince's relocation to a substantially larger and more comprehensive headquarters in San Francisco.
Partner with the relocation project manager, architects, construction teams, designers, IT, Security, and executive leadership to ensure a successful transition.
Develop and execute a comprehensive facilities operational-readiness plan for the new headquarters.
Oversee building systems commissioning, operational testing, inspections, and facilities handover.
Establish required maintenance programs, vendor contracts, workplace services, and operating procedures prior to occupancy.
Ensure the new headquarters supports a significantly larger employee population and more complex workplace services.
Coordinate the readiness of conference facilities, employee amenities, shared spaces, and sample and fabric library areas.
Develop staffing plans, operating budgets, and service standards appropriate for the new facility.
Lead post-occupancy stabilization and establish a scalable facilities operating model.
2. Headquarters Operations & Maintenance
Own day-to-day facilities operations, ensuring a safe, clean, functional, and professionally maintained workplace.
Oversee HVAC, electrical, plumbing, lighting, elevators, building management systems, and other critical infrastructure.
Develop preventive and predictive maintenance programs to maximize reliability and minimize disruptions.
Manage janitorial services, repairs, waste management, pest control, and general building maintenance.
Establish a centralized work-order management system with defined service-level expectations.
Ensure facilities issues are resolved with urgency and accountability.
3. Workplace Experience & Employee Services
Create and maintain a headquarters environment that reflects Quince's brand, culture, and commitment to excellence.
Oversee conference rooms, meeting facilities, kitchens, breakrooms, common areas, and employee amenities.
Manage food, beverage, coffee, snack, and related workplace service programs as applicable.
Partner with IT to ensure meeting spaces and audiovisual systems remain functional.
Support company meetings, leadership events, and headquarters activities.
Continuously improve employee workplace experience through responsive service and thoughtful facilities management.
4. Sample & Fabric Library Management
Directly manage and develop a team of Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators responsible for the organization, tracking, storage, and movement of product samples and fabric materials.
Establish and enforce standardized procedures for sample intake, labeling, cataloging, storage, checkout, transfers, and disposition.
Maintain highly accurate sample and fabric inventories, ensuring materials are properly identified, recorded, and readily accessible.
Implement inventory control systems and periodic physical audits to maintain sample inventory accuracy above 95% .
Partner with Merchandising, Design, Product Development, and other stakeholders to ensure samples and fabrics are available when needed.
Establish clear accountability for missing, misplaced, damaged, or incorrectly cataloged samples.
Optimize library layouts, storage capacity, organization, and retrieval processes within the new headquarters.
Oversee the relocation and accurate reconciliation of existing sample and fabric inventories into the new facility.
Develop KPIs and reporting for sample accuracy, retrieval efficiency, inventory discrepancies, and library service levels.
Continuously improve sample handling processes to reduce loss, improve accessibility, and increase operational efficiency.
5. Financial Management & Cost Optimization
Develop and manage annual headquarters facilities operating budgets and capital expenditure plans.
Establish financial models and operating budgets for the larger headquarters facility.
Maintain financial controls over utilities, maintenance, contracted services, workplace amenities, and capital projects.
Identify cost efficiencies without compromising workplace quality or operational reliability.
Negotiate competitive vendor agreements and monitor performance.
Develop multiyear capital maintenance and infrastructure replacement plans.
Provide regular financial reporting, forecasts, and variance analyses.
6. Vendor & Contract Management
Select, negotiate, and manage third-party facilities service providers.
Establish measurable service-level agreements and performance expectations.
Conduct vendor performance reviews and implement corrective actions when necessary.
Ensure contractors comply with safety, insurance, regulatory, and company requirements.
Maintain productive relationships with landlords, property management, building engineers, and service providers.
7. Safety, Security & Regulatory Compliance
Ensure compliance with applicable building, fire, life-safety, accessibility, environmental, and workplace regulations.
Partner with Security, People, Legal, and IT to maintain physical security and workplace safety programs.
Oversee emergency preparedness, evacuation procedures, and facilities-related business continuity planning.
Coordinate required inspections, permits, certifications, and regulatory documentation.
Proactively identify and mitigate facilities-related operational and safety risks.
8. Space Planning & Facilities Strategy
Partner with leadership to anticipate future space requirements and organizational growth.
Optimize workstations, conference rooms, shared spaces, employee amenities, and sample and fabric library storage.
Coordinate office reconfigurations, furniture installations, and internal moves.
Establish systems to track space utilization, facilities assets, and capital investments.
Develop a multiyear facilities strategy balancing employee experience, operating costs, capacity, and infrastructure reliability.
9. Team Leadership & Operational Excellence
Build and lead a high-performing facilities organization appropriate for the scale and complexity of the new headquarters.
Directly manage the Sample and Fabric Library Coordinators, establishing clear responsibilities, productivity expectations, inventory accuracy standards, and development plans.
Establish operating procedures, performance expectations, and escalation protocols across facilities and library operations.
Implement technology for maintenance management, asset tracking, sample inventory management, vendor oversight, and reporting.
Create a culture of urgency, accountability, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
Establish measurable KPIs and regularly report performance to leadership.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
10+ years of progressive facilities management or corporate real estate operations experience.
5+ years of leadership experience managing large, complex corporate office environments.
Demonstrated experience operating a major corporate headquarters or similarly sophisticated commercial facility.
Direct experience supporting a major headquarters relocation, new building opening, or large-scale office transition.
Strong understanding of commercial building systems, preventive maintenance, workplace services, and life-safety requirements.
Experience developing and managing significant operating budgets and capital expenditures.
Proven success managing complex vendor relationships and service contracts.
Experience leading operational teams with measurable service and inventory accuracy expectations.
Strong project management, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to operate effectively in a rapidly growing organization.
Exceptional attention to detail, responsiveness, and commitment to operational excellence.
Preferred
Experience managing corporate headquarters facilities exceeding 100,000 square feet.
Experience transitioning organizations into substantially larger or more complex headquarters environments.
Background in high-growth technology, e-commerce, consumer products, or retail organizations.
Experience overseeing product sample rooms, fabric libraries, inventory control, or similar operational functions.
Experience establishing facilities operations for newly constructed or renovated commercial buildings.
Familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), building management systems (BMS), and inventory management technology.
Professional certifications such as Certified Facility Manager (CFM) or Facility Management Professional (FMP).
Knowledge of San Francisco building codes, regulatory requirements, and commercial property operations.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Lifting up to 50 pounds
Standing and walking throughout the entirety of your shift
Ability to go up and down stairs, use of ladders throughout the day as needed
Bending, twisting, or kneeling may be required throughout the day for lifting or maneuvering objects
May be asked to work outside or travel to shoots off-site as needed

ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Senior Recruiter, Campus
Own Quince's campus and early-career recruiting execution from attraction through assessment and closing, and partner with Talent and business leaders on hiring plans, school priorities and process design across MBA and undergraduate pipelines in Engineering, Product and business functions.
Core responsibilities
Help create the campus strategy: partner with Talent and business leaders on hiring plans, school priorities and the annual recruiting calendar.
Own full-cycle recruiting: applications, recruiter screens, assessments, interviews, offers and closing across MBA and undergraduate programs, with candidate ownership through acceptance.
Lead technical campus recruiting: partner with Engineering on candidate profiles, create and lead full assessment process including technical interviews, and credibly sell Quince Engineering to CS students.
Deliver attraction events: info sessions, coffee chats, tech talks and Palo Alto HQ events for both undergraduate and MBA schools, with functional leaders and recent hires.
Build school relationships and pipelines: career centers, student organizations, alumni and school champions; primary day-to-day contact for all target schools.
Run the assessment process: review batches, batched interview days, Bar Raiser coordination, interviewer capacity and calibration with hiring teams, with logistics support in peak periods.
Own reporting and retro inputs: Greenhouse accuracy, pipeline conversion by school and function, candidate experience, weekly pipeline readout.
Launch approved expansions: internship, functional or geographic pipelines with clear delivery and resource plans.
Experience
5+ years recruiting experience in tech hiring, with a working foundation in how engineering roles are assessed; ideally campus recruiting in that space.
Campus or early-career recruiting experience, ideally across undergraduate technical and MBA populations.
Builder profile: creates process and pipeline where none exists and is comfortable with a late, compressed cycle.
Strong assessment, candidate management, stakeholder partnership and closing skills.
Experience managing high-volume seasonal cycles in a fast-moving environment.
Greenhouse, Handshake and CodeSignal.

THE ROLE
Software Development Engineer in Test II, (SDET II)
We are seeking a high-impact SDET II to join our growing team. This role goes beyond traditional testing: you will own quality end-to-end, from test strategy and automation through CI/CD, performance, and data validation. You will work closely with engineering, product, and DevOps to ship high-quality releases, shorten feedback cycles, and keep production reliable. In this role, you will help the team move faster with confidence by building scalable automation, catching defects early, and raising the quality bar across the organization.
Responsibilities
Design and scale robust automation frameworks for web, API, and mobile, using Playwright or Selenium with Java, Python, or TypeScript and a POM-based architecture.
Target 75–85% automation coverage of critical flows and keep flaky tests under 5% in the regression suite.
Own critical user journeys end-to-end across UI, API, database, and analytics layers,
including cart, checkout, and subscriptions. Validate functional behavior, business logic, event tracking accuracy, and data integrity.
Build comprehensive test strategies, not just test cases. Cover functional, regression, integration, and exploratory testing, plus localization, content, cross-browser, and cross-device validation, and apply shift-left practices.
Design and execute load and stress tests with Locust or JMeter, simulating incremental, spike, and real-user traffic patterns.
Analyze response times, throughput, and error rates to identify bottlenecks and recommend optimizations.
Validate PII handling and masking across UI and API, and check for sensitive data leakage, secure headers, and basic security issues.
Integrate automated regression and smoke tests into CI/CD pipelines such as Bitbucket
Pipelines, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions. Maintain pipeline stability at 90% or higher and keep smoke validation under 15 minutes.
Build test reporting dashboards, failure analytics, and trend tracking using tools like ReportPortal, Allure, Slack alerts, and custom dashboards, and turn the results into actionable insights for stakeholders.
Participate in sprint planning, grooming, and retrospectives. Mentor junior QA engineers and SDETs, and help drive a quality-first culture.
Qualifications
Required:
3–5 years of experience in QA or SDET roles, with strong programming skills in Java, Python, TypeScript, or JavaScript
Hands-on experience with Playwright or Selenium, TestNG, JUnit, or PyTest, and API testing tools such as REST Assured, Postman, or custom frameworks
Experience with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, Bitbucket Pipelines, or GitHub Actions, and proficiency with Git
Strong test design, root cause analysis, and debugging skills across UI, API, and network layers
Experience with SQL-based database validation and event or analytics validation
Understanding of distributed systems basics, API performance, and load testing tools such as Locust or JMeter
Solid grasp of SDLC, STLC, and Agile methodologies
Strong analytical thinking, an ownership mindset, and clear communication with stakeholders
Preferred:
Experience in e-commerce or high-traffic systems
Advanced Playwright features such as network interception and tracing
Performance engineering experience, including spike and endurance testing
Security validation basics
Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and observability tools such as Grafana or Kibana

Staff Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET)

Define and drive the SDET and test automation strategy across multiple products and engineering teams.
Architect, build, and maintain scalable automation frameworks for UI (app and web), API, integration, end-to-end, and service-level testing.
